bib.title: SELFCHECKGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models

question: Can hallucinations in black-box LLM responses be detected without an external database or token probabilities, by checking consistency across stochastically sampled responses?
hypothesis: If an LLM knows a concept, sampled responses are similar and consistent; for hallucinated facts, samples diverge and contradict one another.
contributions: SelfCheckGPT, a sampling-based zero-resource black-box hallucination detector with five consistency variants (BERTScore, QA, n-gram, NLI, Prompt)
An annotated dataset of 238 GPT-3 generated WikiBio passages with sentence-level factuality labels
Comparison with grey-box (token probability/entropy) and proxy-LLM baselines at sentence and passage level

method.summary: GPT-3 generates passages about WikiBio concepts; sentences are annotated for factuality by hand. Each sentence of the greedy response is scored for inconsistency against N=20 temperature-1.0 samples using BERTScore, MQAG question answering, an n-gram model, DeBERTa NLI, or an LLM yes/no prompt, and compared with token-probability baselines.
method.task: sentence-level hallucination detection and passage-level factuality ranking

datasets.name: WikiBio GPT-3 (new, annotated)
datasets.source: 238 concepts sampled randomly from the top 20% longest paragraphs of the WikiBio test set (Lebret et al., 2016); passages generated by GPT-3; released on project page
datasets.preprocessing: Labels: major inaccurate 761 (39.9%), minor inaccurate 631 (33.1%), accurate 516 (27.0%). 201 sentences double-annotated, disagreements resolved to worst-case label. Cohen's kappa 0.595 (3-class), 0.748 (2-class). Passage score = mean of sentence labels (1, 0.5, 0). NonFact* = major-inaccurate detection in 206 non-total-hallucination passages (1632 sentences).

other.use: passage generator, grey-box baseline (top-5 token probs), and Prompt checker
SelfCheckGPT-Prompt checker, system message 'You are a helpful assistant.'

models.name: T5-Large G1 (SQuAD) and G2 (RACE); Longformer answerer (RACE); Longformer answerability (SQuAD2.0)

other.use: proxy LLMs for token probability/entropy; LLaMA-30B in main table

inference.decoding: main response: temperature 0.0 with standard beam search; samples: stochastic sampling at temperature 1.0
inference.samples: N=20 samples per passage; one run, no seeds or significance tests stated; ablation with N=4 for LLM choice
inference.prompting: Generation prompt 'This is a Wikipedia passage about {concept}:'; check prompt in prompts block; zero-shot
inference.retrieval: none (zero-resource); ablation uses the WikiBio first paragraph as reference

parameters.QA answerability: soft-counting with alpha, no threshold value stated
parameters.NLI: logits of entailment and contradiction only
parameters.n-gram: model trained on the N samples plus the response; best 1-gram max
parameters.entropy: GPT-3 API top-5 token probabilities only

other.cost: Prompt over 1908 sentences x 20 samples about $200 (GPT-3, $0.020/1k tokens) and $20 (ChatGPT, $0.002/1k tokens)
other.prompt_output_rate: GPT-3 outputs Yes or No 98% of the time

metrics.name: AUC-PR (sentence level)
metrics.definition: Area under precision-recall curve for detecting non-factual (major+minor), non-factual* (major only in non-total-hallucination passages) and factual sentences

metrics.name: Pearson / Spearman correlation (passage level)
metrics.definition: Correlation of mean sentence score with human passage score

baselines: GPT-3 Avg/Max of -log p and entropy (grey-box)
LLaMA and other proxy LLM probabilities/entropy
WikiBio reference paragraph in place of samples (ablation)
eval.protocol: Single evaluation on 238 passages with one human-annotated label set; no confidence intervals or seeds.

availability.data: released on project page (annotated WikiBio GPT-3 dataset)

limits: Only 238 passages, predominantly about individuals from WikiBio; no locations or objects (authors' Limitations)
Sentence-level labelling: a sentence can mix factual and non-factual content; atomic-fact scoring (FActScore) left for later
SelfCheckGPT-Prompt is best but computationally heavy
Generator is text-davinci-003 only; checker models (GPT-3, ChatGPT) are now dated; LLaMA and ChatGPT-style models not tested as generators
Label scheme gives 39.9% major-inaccurate and a peak of total-hallucination passages, so base rate is high (random AUC-PR 72.96 for non-factual)
No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; gains between close variants (Prompt vs NLI) are untested
Detects inconsistency, not falsehood: a model consistently wrong would pass
